_format: skill-creator eval format. Run each prompt in a fresh session with and without the skill; grade the assertions. expect_trigger false marks a should-not-trigger probe.

evals.prompt: I want our developer tool to go viral. We have about 25 short explainer videos for different audiences. Where do I post what?
assertions: Assigns platforms by job: short vertical clips for discovery, the full videos for buyers, the runnable product for Show HN
Says Show HN must be something people can run or try, not a video or landing page
Proposes a launch order (developer and humour pieces first, leadership last) rather than posting everything at once
Defines success as stayed-to-watch, comments from target roles and click-through, not impressions
Does not promise virality or quote invented benchmarks

evals.prompt: Turn our 90 second explainer into Shorts.
assertions: One tension per Short, taken from the long video's strongest lines
The hook lands in the first two seconds as on-screen words and voice together, without a logo intro
Captions burned in inside the safe area
Links each Short to the long video as its related video
Suggests testing two or three openings and comparing stayed-to-watch against the channel's own earlier Shorts

evals.prompt: Write a hook for our AI agent tool: 'Revolutionary AI that 10x's your developers'.
assertions: Pushes back on the hype wording and explains developers distrust it, citing the scepticism evidence
Offers hooks that name a concrete developer pain instead (for example reviewing more pull requests than anyone can read)
Keeps claims verifiable and labels demos or comparisons honestly

evals.prompt: I want tongue-in-cheek Shorts that troll a bit, poke at 'agentic engineering' and 'swarms'. Give me three ideas.
assertions: Aims the humour at the situation, the hype vocabulary or the brand's unimportant traits, never at a group of people or a named competitor
Signals the joke visually in the first two seconds instead of pure deadpan
Ends each idea on a real product screen or a labelled demo to repay credibility
Ties each joke to the product so it would not work without it
Warns that claims sounding measured must be provable and that a recognisable competitor makes it comparative advertising

evals.prompt: Our Shorts get views but people swipe away. How do we make people stay?
assertions: Says view counts count every start and judges on stayed to watch, engaged views and average % viewed against the channel's own baseline
Puts the product doing the thing in the first frame instead of a logo or intro card
Says the name early without a big centred logo and uses brief brand pulses
Recommends keyword supers over full captions while a diagram is on screen and making the first 3 s work muted
Marks hook-type and cut-cadence rules as tests because no study supports a fixed cadence

evals.prompt: How do I find out if anyone actually wants this, using the videos we made per audience?
assertions: Measures a ladder of behaviour (visit, qualified signup, call, letter of intent or pilot) rather than views or likes
Gives each audience its own spoken short web address because Shorts links are not clickable
Asks for thresholds and kill criteria written down before launch, with a fixed window and no peeking
Says small traffic cannot A/B-test landing pages and compares each audience against its threshold
Mentions consent for waitlist email and cookieless analytics in the EU

evals.prompt: Our Kubernetes ingress returns 502s after the last deploy. Where do I look first?
assertions: Does not invoke devtool-social; answers about ingress and backend health
